title: CRITICAL: worker containers fail their probe and the reason is thrown away
description:
Per-tick container fan-out has never once succeeded. Reproduced three times on 2026-08-22 against the live factory, including with a single worker so contention is not a factor:

  07:34:31.208  dispatched
  07:34:33.063  task-started - worker container dispatched for 3nh
  07:34:54.615  cloud_reconcile:1:1 never-dispatched
  07:34:54.746  handoff:closeout

23 seconds against a 418-second probe budget, so this is NOT the 7go timeout — the probe RAN and failed. The timing matches a warm boot (17.8s measured by kuf) plus a fast probe failure. Manifests are written with a real process_id, so startProcess returned; the container came up and ticks-worker --probe did not print WORKER_PROBE_MARKER.

TWO DEFECTS, AND THE SECOND IS WHY THE FIRST IS STILL OPEN.

1. The probe fails. Leading hypothesis, unconfirmed: the Dockerfile verifies ticks-worker --probe at BUILD time with the container default environment, and it passes there. At runtime the dispatcher calls startProcess(command, {env: workerBootEnv(...)}). If the real Sandbox SDK REPLACES the process environment rather than merging it, PATH is lost — the absolute path to ticks-worker still resolves, but the tk, git and harness lookups inside its probe do not, and it exits without the marker. FakeSandboxes does not model that, which is why 533 tests are green. Verify against the SDK before writing code; do not trust this hypothesis.

2. The probe output is discarded. ProbeOutcome.output holds exactly what the container said and nothing persists it — not to R2 beside the manifest, not to the dispatch log, not to a run event. So a failed probe is unexplainable after the fact, and diagnosing it costs a live paid run plus wrangler tail (which captured 6,625 HTTP records and none of the Workflow console output). FIX THIS FIRST, then re-run once and read the answer. The orchestrator burned three runs and roughly \$3-4 guessing at what one persisted string would have said.

Also fix the misleading verdict: reconcile reports never-dispatched for a container that WAS dispatched and did answer. Same class as 074 and c5i — technically true, reliably misread.
notes:
2026-08-22 10:05 - Do the observability half FIRST and independently — persist the probe's captured output beside the worker manifest in R2, surface it in the dispatch log or a run event, and make reconcile stop calling a container that answered 'never-dispatched'. That work stands on its own merit whatever the cause turns out to be, and it is what lets the next live run answer the question instead of costing another one. Only then chase the probe failure itself.

Everything already known is in the tick description. The one thing worth re-reading before coding: cloud/sandbox/Dockerfile line ~255 runs ticks-worker --probe at build time and greps for the marker, and that passes — so the difference is runtime, not the image.

So PATH from the image's own ENV should survive. Do not carry that hypothesis forward; the next live run's persisted probe_failure.output is the evidence to read instead.

Cause of the gap, found by grep: probe_failure is written from cloud/factory/src/reconcile.ts:644 only. The path that actually produces this failure — spawnWorker's probe outcome inside dispatchWave — does not persist it. So the observability half instrumented reconcile rather than the probe, and the question the tick existed to answer is still unanswered after two more live runs.

Persist it where the ProbeOutcome is produced, not only where reconcile reports a classification. Note also that the earlier run_67b0ad89 attempt captured the PREVIOUS image because it was submitted while tk factory deploy was still rolling out — a run pins its image at submission, so always wait for 'Factory ready' before dispatching a diagnostic run.
2026-08-22 10:44 - Reopened: the tick's own acceptance — that the next live run produces a readable answer — is not met.
2026-08-22 10:54 - RE-DISPATCH BRIEF. Your predecessor landed probe_failure persistence in reconcile.ts:644 only, and the path that actually fails — spawnWorker's ProbeOutcome inside dispatchWave — still discards its output. Two more live runs produced no answer because of it. Do not repeat that.

THE ONE THING THIS TICK MUST DELIVER: ProbeOutcome.output persisted where it is PRODUCED, so a failing probe explains itself. Pin it with a test that drives a FAILING probe through dispatchWave and asserts the captured output reaches the manifest — a test that only covers reconcile's classification is how this shipped half-done the first time.

WHAT IS ALREADY RULED OUT, with evidence — do not re-investigate:
- 7go's probe budget: it is 418s and the failure is at 21s, so the probe returns early rather than timing out.
- PATH loss: your predecessor read @cloudflare/sandbox@0.12.7's types; env extends BaseExecOptions and overrides per-key rather than replacing, so the image's own ENV survives.
- A stale bundle: the deployed code changed observably (the dispatch-log label moved from cloud_reconcile: to cloud_reconcile_plan:).
- Contention: reproduces with a single worker.
- A broken image: cloud/sandbox/Dockerfile runs ticks-worker --probe at build time and greps for the marker, and that passes.

THE SHAPE OF THE FAILURE, six runs, always the same: the container is addressed, startProcess returns a real process_id which is written to the manifest, and roughly 21 seconds later the wave reports never-dispatched with collect correctly finding no branch on origin. 21s is close to a warm boot (kuf measured 17.8s) plus a few seconds, which is why the probe running and failing fits better than the probe never starting — but treat that as a lead, not a conclusion.

SECOND, SMALLER FIX WORTH DOING HERE: reconcile reports never-dispatched for a container that was demonstrably dispatched and answered. Same misleading-signal class as 074 and c5i.

OPERATIONAL NOTE that cost a run: a run pins its image at SUBMISSION, so a diagnostic run dispatched while tk factory deploy is still rolling out silently uses the previous image. Wait for 'Factory ready'.

Both previous attempts instrumented a branch the live failure did not take; an array returned by the call cannot be branch-dependent. Written to artifacts/wave/<batch>.json.

Also correcting the orchestrator's own misreading, which ys3 had already fixed and I kept getting wrong across four runs: cloud_reconcile_plan:1:1 never-dispatched is the PRE-DISPATCH snapshot, drawn before the batch's containers are addressed and logged afterwards. It is not a verdict. The real signal is task-completed no-commits — the worker did not push a branch — and I had no evidence the probe failed at all.
